overlap.title: The two goats have distinct roles
overlap.summary: One goat is killed for the offering; the other is sent alive into the wilderness.
overlap.reasoning: The two actions belong to different animals within one procedure. The passage explicitly instructs release of the live goat; it does not describe killing both.
overlap.scope: This identifies the stated ritual sequence. The meaning of Azazel, comparative ritual history and later practices require further research; the text alone does not establish a physical mechanism of removing guilt.

checks.overlapDecision: Distinct Q about the meaning and referent of the second lot, not a repeat of the published two-goat ritual sequence; that record flags further research but does not set out these identity alternatives. No H/G inferred from unsettled meaning.

overlap.title: Festival lengths and evening boundaries
overlap.summary: The calendar distinguishes an evening boundary from a daytime date, and seven days in booths from an eighth-day assembly.
overlap.reasoning: The surrounding instructions explain why the ninth evening and tenth day, or seven festival days and an eighth assembly, need not be competing totals.
overlap.scope: This reading addresses these particular dates. It does not settle ancient calendar disputes, the meaning of Sabbath in the harvest count, or correspondence with modern dates.

overlap.title: The festival burnt-offering lists specify different bull and ram counts
overlap.summary: Numbers prescribes two bulls and one ram; Leviticus’s offering with the firstfruits bread specifies one bull and two rams.
overlap.reasoning: Separate offerings for different aspects of the same festival could account for both lists. The passages do not explicitly identify these two lists as additions to one another; Numbers explicitly names only the continual offering as additional here.
overlap.scope: This is a comparison of prescribed lists, not proof that historical sacrifices conflicted. A cumulative reading is possible but requires interpretation.

checks.overlapDecision: Reviewed overlapping records and all ENTRIES studies: different finding, not duplicate.

overlap.title: Different legal treatment of servants and slaves
overlap.summary: The laws distinguish servants by origin and family status, preserve ownership claims, and specify some release conditions.
overlap.reasoning: The broad Jubilee proclamation must be read alongside the explicit foreign-slavery provision. Israelite redemption protections do not establish equivalent release for everyone.
overlap.scope: These unequal legal categories do not establish how consistently the laws were practiced. The scope of the broad liberty proclamation merits further study.
